speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. To begin our assessment, have you noticed any specific pattern to the rash, such as whether it is itchy, painful, or if it spreads in a linear fashion?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with a rash that started last night, finding it very concerning. He does not recall being exposed to any new environmental stimuli such as detergents or plants like poison ivy. He mentions he recently started seeing a primary care provider for arthritis management and a new onset cough.

speaker: Doctor
text: That cough is significant; is it dry or productive, and do you have any shortness of breath or chest pain? Additionally, have you noticed any fever, joint swelling, or fatigue accompanying this rash?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on the upper half of the back. I also have Concern over sudden onset, Recent cough, Unaware of exposure to new environmental stimuli, Mucositis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) and Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR).
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug Eruption Secondary to Rheumatoid Arthritis Treatment (likely Methotrexate toxicity given the new cough and mucositis).
